The dominant single-sector event was CMS-6098-P, proposed 2026-11-16, which would extrapolate Medicare Advantage RADV audits back to payment year 2018: UNH -10.21%, HUM -12.98%, CVS -5.20%, XLV -2.20%, with the comment period open until 2027-01-19. data_quality_notes: Research ran 06:01-06:38 ET of a ~60 minute budget and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so nothing was lost to the clock. Five ideas is the whole output and the count is deliberate. WHY FIVE: the prior record is 5/44 to target (11%), avg -5.5%, with single-name swing stock longs at 2/30 (7%) and long_term 0/4 at -15.2%. 44 closed is past the noise threshold, so the bar was raised rather than the count matched. Roughly 35 names were screened; open-market insider buying appeared in six (DKS, DY, ADSK, LEN, HUN, ADM) and only DKS and DY also had a dated catalyst and levels clearing both the 2.0 ATR stop floor and the R:R floor. Every rejection has its arithmetic written down in notes.md - XLV, ADSK, WMT and the whole de-rated batch failed because a 2.0 ATR stop plus a 2.0 R:R forces a target 4 ATR above entry, which for names only 5-12% off their highs would have to print above the range high. RATIO HONESTY: DKS sits at exactly 2.00, on the floor rather than above it - it is an existing filled position whose entry cannot be amended, so the target was not fitted to a new entry, but a reader should treat an exactly-at-floor ratio as the weakest of the five. The three long-term ideas cluster at 2.81-2.86 against a 2.5 floor; CVS discloses its own sensitivity, failing outright at 2.45 if the target multiple is 12.5x rather than 13.0x. Both stop distances were re-fetched at synthesis: DKS 15.50 risk = 2.47 ATR (ATR14 6.2649), DY 27.78 risk = 2.09 ATR (ATR14 13.2761), both clearing the 2.0 stock-swing floor. CONCENTRATION: three of five ideas are healthcare, 8.0% of capital if all fill (UNH 3.0 + CVS 2.5 + PFE 2.5). UNH and CVS are the same bet - both de-rated by CMS-6098-P on the same session - which is 2 on one driver against a cap of 3; XLV was rejected so nothing else joins them. PFE is not on that driver (it fell 1.44% on a day UNH fell 10.21%) but is the same sector, and its entry is a target cut on an existing position rather than new risk. The concentration stands because the alternatives failed their floors: ADM and HUN were both worked through in a final pass and both are on the watchlist with the arithmetic shown. HORIZON MIX: 2 swing, 3 long_term, 0 intraday. Not manufactured - the only same-session catalysts were this morning's prints (WMT, BABA, ROAD) and there is no pre-market data at 6am; every price in this report is the 2026-11-18 close. SOURCES THAT FAILED: market_data.py macro returned zero bytes after running most of the session, so there is NO fetched read on rates, VIX, DXY or any FRED series - the regime call above is built from ETF and commodity-proxy closes instead, which is weaker. market_data.py events is broken rather than quiet: 'Fed' returns Kalshi sports parlays matching the substring 'Federico', 'CPI' returns a football parlay, four other macro queries return count 0, and every market returned has null yes_ask, last_price and volume - hence no event-contract idea. market_data.py implied returned yahoo-options HTTP 401 on every symbol, so the 'is the target inside the options-implied move' test could not be run on any idea at all. market_data.py short returned a nasdaq ReadTimeout, so there is no short-interest read anywhere. history failed for GES, SLP and LESL. NOT COVERED: no futures idea, and that is a tooling gap rather than a judgement - no futures quote path returned a price, and setting levels on /MES, /MGC or /MCL from an ETF proxy would be inventing a contract price. The macro picture (gold at a 150-day low, crude broken, bonds bid) was the clearest futures setup in weeks and went untraded for want of a feed. No crypto idea: BTC, ETH and SOL were all flat on the day and IBIT is -28.4% from its high in a straight line, which is a knife to buy and late to short. No primary filings were read this morning - the DY counter-argument rests on secondary sources and says so in its own evidence block. TWO STANDING ORDERS SHOULD BE RETIRED, not re-pitched: GLD SELL @ 406.77 (16.1% above the market) and /MBTZ6 SHORT @ 74,075 (~16% above spot). Both are on the watchlist with reasons. ADM traded 67.52-68.77 on 11/18, entirely below its 68.80 buy entry, so that order may have filled without the state file reflecting it - flagged rather than assumed. See market_context.summary for the two position closes (BCC, OXY) that could not be expressed as candidates. === RED TEAM (phase 2c) === Cut 2 of 5, kept 3, downgraded every one of the three kept. CUT UNH (rank 2, the largest position in the report at 3%): its 2.86 reward-to-risk is built on a 285.74 bear case called conservative for sitting below the 317.135 150-day low, but UNH printed a low under 285.74 on 36 sessions this year and bottomed at 255.965 on 2026-03-27 - against a downside the stock has actually traded, the ratio is 1.47:1. This is the same move as walking a stop in, done with the bear case: the window was short enough to make the denominator small. The 408.20 target compounds it at 20.0x, a round number whose only justification is the multiple UNH held two sessions ago, and the ratio fails at 19.0x. CUT PFE (rank 5): the report correctly identified that a 42.00 target is unsupportable and then replaced it with 36.60, which is 12.0x and still above any multiple the stock has carried in 150 days - nothing anchors 12.0x, and at the 10.31x the stock has actually been paid the ratio is 1.20:1. Its own key_risk concedes the LOE schedule was never fetched, so the question that decides the idea went unexamined. The target cut is right and is carried in market_context.summary as a position instruction, because the position is open and would otherwise keep the 42.00. DOWNGRADED DY 5 to 3: the conviction-5 claim does not survive its own evidence. The technical_level item asserted 'a rising sequence of session lows' built by omitting the 11/11 and 11/12 lows (220.88, 222.86 - the two highest) and placing 11/16 before 11/17; the real structure is a six-session base with the 11/16 low below the 11/10 low. The catalyst asserted 'the bar has already been reset downward' when the fetched figures show the company guided to a 4.56 midpoint against a 4.68 consensus midpoint - guided below, not reset - and no current consensus was fetched. Both are corrected in place. The valuation case (14.69x on 4-of-4 beats, -60.1% off the high) is intact and is why DY is still rank 1. DOWNGRADED CVS 4 to 3: it discloses that its 2.84 becomes 2.45 and fails at a 12.5x target, and nothing separates 13.0x from 12.5x; and $350.7M of net insider selling runs against the insider-buying screen that put the other two ideas in the report. It is kept, and promoted to rank 2, because it is the only idea this morning whose downside is honest - 66.64 is below a price CVS has not traded under in 200 sessions, the test UNH failed. DOWNGRADED DKS 4 to 3: its technical_level described the close rather than the tape, which is six consecutive lower lows into the print (147.51 to 140.05), and its expectancy is +0.14R on 4.7 points of claimed edge at an R:R of exactly 2.00. It amends no stored level, so its only content is the trim instruction, now mirrored into market_context. TWO VALIDATOR ARTIFACTS, recorded rather than worked around. First, the sources check 404s on api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical for DY, UNH, DKS and PFE. That is the endpoint market_data.py calls with query parameters, not a hallucinated URL - the OHLCV behind it was re-fetched this phase and every 150-day high, low, SMA and ATR in the report matches to the cent. The citations are re-pointed at www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/<sym>/historical, which serves the same data and returns 200 to a reader. Second, the spread check fails DY at 9.38% and DKS at 13.50% off a 6:41am book: DY's bid of 228.00 is above its own 225.78 close, and DKS's quote is stamped 'Nov 18, 2026' with no time at all - it is the prior session's closing book, not a live spread, on a name trading $300M a day. check_spread handles a missing book as normal outside regular hours but treats a stale one as real; it is the only check in the set with no session awareness. Those two rows may still be demoted at enforcement on a measurement that is not about the trade, which is why the DKS instruction was mirrored. Not changed, because changing the validator to pass the report's own ideas is the thing this phase exists to prevent - it is a code fix with a test, for a day that is not this one. THREE IDEAS REMAIN: DY, CVS, DKS. Capital at risk if all fill falls from 12.0% to 6.5%, healthcare from three names and 8.0% to one name and 2.5%, and the CMS-6098-P cluster from two names to one. No idea in this report now carries a conviction above 3. Validation demoted 2 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 1 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

recommendations.thesis: Four fetched quarters of actual EPS - 2.09, 2.58, 2.57 and 1.09 - sum to $8.33 trailing, and CVS beat the estimate in all four. The 81.35 close is 9.77x and the 77.50 entry is 9.30x, against 17.14x for UNH on the same fetched-TTM method. Both are being sold on the same CMS proposal and this one is already at 9.3x. The 108.29 target is 13.0x, a small discount to the 13.29x the stock itself carried at its 110.68 high inside the last 150 days, on earnings it has already reported rather than earnings it has to grow into.
recommendations.key_risk: Two things the valuation does not answer, and they are why this is 2.5% and not larger. First, insiders are net sellers of $350,741,379 over six months - 8 sells against a single $2,001,315 purchase - and Glenview Capital was reported cutting its position into this selloff. Second, this report already owned CVS and was stopped out of it on 2026-11-04; buying it again 10% lower on a different horizon is a deliberate decision, not an oversight, and if it is wrong it will be wrong twice. EXPLICIT INVALIDATION (a price fall is not one): trailing-four-quarter reported EPS below $6.50 for two consecutive quarters, or CVS abandons the announced breakup, or it withdraws full-year guidance citing RADV liabilities. The 66.64 bear price is 8.0x trailing EPS, below the 9.14x the 150-day low of 76.10 represents.
recommendations.counter_argument: The bear case is that CVS is the worst-placed name in the group, not the cheapest: Aetna carries the MA audit exposure, the planned breakup is unresolved, and the people who know the company best sold $350.7M of it. Answered with the only comparison that is measurable: CVS trades at 9.77x trailing EPS having beaten four of four quarters, while UNH, hit by the identical rule on the identical day, trades at 17.14x having beaten three of four. The audit risk is discounted roughly twice as hard here. The honest weakness is sensitivity - at a 12.5x target instead of 13.0x the reward-to-risk is 2.45 and this idea fails the 2.5 long-term floor outright. It survives on half a turn of multiple, and the reader should size it knowing that. RED TEAM: the UNH leg of that comparison was cut this phase, so the 'same rule, same day, half the multiple' argument now stands without its other half published - the arithmetic is unchanged and still correct, but it is a relative claim and the reader no longer has the relative trade. Two things lower the score to 3. First, the sensitivity this idea discloses about itself is the whole margin: 2.84 at a 13.0x target, 2.45 and failing at 12.5x, and nothing in the evidence distinguishes 13.0x from 12.5x - a ratio that lives inside half a turn of a judgment call is not a 4. Second, positioning runs against the thesis. Insider buying is this report's own primary screen - it is why DY and DKS are here - and CVS shows $350.7M of net insider selling, 8 sells against one $2.0M buy. Applying a screen as a positive when it hits and ignoring it when it misses is not a screen. What keeps CVS in the report is that it is the only idea this morning whose downside is honest: the 66.64 bear case is below a price the stock has not traded under on any of the last 200 sessions (200-day low 69.5101, 2026-03-30), which is the test UNH failed.
